title: Transcriptomic Analysis of Endolysosomal Trafficking Machinery Reveals Dynamic Expression Patterns Among SNX, RAB, MON1, and VPS Genes During Human Osteoclast Differentiation
content:
Background/Objectives: Endolysosomal trafficking is essential for osteoclast function, yet transcriptional differences among individual trafficking-associated genes during differentiation remain incompletely characterized. We investigated these differences and their consistency across independent osteoclast transcriptomic datasets.
Methods: Human RNA-sequencing datasets GSE246769 (primary differentiation time course) and GSE225974 (independent dataset) were analyzed alongside mouse dataset GSE147174 for exploratory cross-species comparisons. Twenty-seven trafficking-associated genes and 11 gene pairs were selected retrospectively based on biological relevance and expression profiles. In GSE246769, gene-pair responses were compared using matched observations from eight donors with Benjamini–Hochberg correction. Additional analyses assessed temporal differences, category-level enrichment, independent support via unpaired Welch tests, and sensitivity across all 40,320 possible sample assignments.
Results: Nine of 11 gene pairs showed significantly different transcriptional responses between days 2 and 9, including a pronounced divergence between SNX25 and SNX30. Eight pairs showed concordant directions and significant differences in GSE225974. Seven remained significant under all 40,320 sample assignments: RAB5A–RAB5B, RAB5B–RAB5C, MON1A–MON1B, SNX10–SNX18, SNX25–SNX30, VPS16–VPS41, and VPS16–VPS8; five also remained significant between days 5 and 9. Five genes (SNX10, SNX18, SNX30, RAB5B, and VPS16) showed significant, concordant changes across human and mouse datasets. No trafficking category met the predefined enrichment criterion.
Conclusions: We identify seven gene-pair transcriptional relationships involving RAB5, MON1, sorting nexin, and VPS genes with consistent statistical support across independent human osteoclast datasets. These findings highlight distinct expression patterns among functionally related trafficking genes and prioritize candidates for future functional investigation.
